No node exists at path '/ns001:system/ns001:versionStorage/cb/d7/b9/cbd7b91e8b5351c421754c4135cfdd1a0ee3b1b8/1.1' in workspace "default"
, does that versionStorage thing seem correct or is this coming from somewhere in the resource?
It seems correct. The version storage is in a separate, system-managed area.
is the one who is most familiar with versioning. You may want to touch base with him as well.
, can you give me a run down on what happens when you create a version. Where is it stored and how is it referenced from the resource?
Is the jcr namespace bound to ns001?  That seems odd to me, but perhaps things have changed since I last explored this area.
As for versioning, it's laid out here (

but basically when you create a version it adds a mixin "mix:versionable" then uses the jcr version manager to create a version snapshot.  The copies of the content exist in the system space "/jcr:system/jcr:versionStorage".  The fedora 4 implementation does a lot of funny business to make those nodes (in the system space) addressable at URIs of the pattern "/original/node/path/fcr:versions/version-label".
I could imagine an issue if the ACL code makes standard JCR assumptions and invokes node.getParent() or something like that.
If we had the line number where the caught exception is thrown that results in the 404 (or the line where we check whether a node exists) it would be easier to debug the issue.
The access error is most likely coming from:
It appears that the error is generated once the response is ready and is being written out by the RdfStreamProvider.
A section of catalina.out for a request
I'm not sure what is changing between the accumulation of the Rdf and the outputting.  Will look closer at RdfStreamingOutputProvider.

The RdfStreams are lazy-loaded. In other words, the content of the various streams are only read when they are used (i.e. when creating the HTTP response). The RdfStreamingOutputProvider shows the error because it is the code that is running through the lazy streams. The actual access error is coming from the VersionsRdfContext... when its stream is actually read.

comments.body:
Ok, I don't fully understand the versioning system. But here is what is causing the 404.

After authenticating against the resource (successfully) and then failing to authenticate against the ACL (resource inaccessible), it seems to want to check the versions.

DEBUG 20:10:41.136 (WebACRolesProvider) findRolesForPath: /{httpwww.jcp.orgjcr1.0}system/{httpwww.jcp.orgjcr1.0}versionStorage/{}cb/{}d7/{}b9/{}cbd7b91e8b5351c421754c4135cfdd1a0ee3b1b8/{}1.1

Which is weird because my resource is at http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/d5/05/20/44/d5052044-1bf6-4217-8445-f00145046082

You can see the error more clearly by trying a PATCH request as the testuser

> echo "PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/> INSERT { <> dc:title \"This is a title\" . } WHERE {}" | curl -i -XPATCH -u"testuser:password1" -H"Content-type: application/sparql-update" --upload-file - "http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/d5/05/20/44/d5052044-1bf6-4217-8445-f00145046082"
HTTP/1.1 100 Continue

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Server: Apache-Coyote/1.1
Cache-Control: private
Expires: Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 UTC
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 136
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2015 20:25:02 GMT
Connection: close

No node exists at path '/ns001:system/ns001:versionStorage/cb/d7/b9/cbd7b91e8b5351c421754c4135cfdd1a0ee3b1b8/1.1' in workspace "default"

Andrew Woods, does that versionStorage thing seem correct or is this coming from somewhere in the resource?
It seems correct. The version storage is in a separate, system-managed area. Michael Durbin is the one who is most familiar with versioning. You may want to touch base with him as well.
Michael Durbin, can you give me a run down on what happens when you create a version. Where is it stored and how is it referenced from the resource?

Is the jcr namespace bound to ns001? That seems odd to me, but perhaps things have changed since I last explored this area.

As for versioning, it's laid out here (http://www.day.com/specs/jcr/2.0/15_Versioning.html), but basically when you create a version it adds a mixin "mix:versionable" then uses the jcr version manager to create a version snapshot. The copies of the content exist in the system space "/jcr:system/jcr:versionStorage". The fedora 4 implementation does a lot of funny business to make those nodes (in the system space) addressable at URIs of the pattern "/original/node/path/fcr:versions/version-label".

I could imagine an issue if the ACL code makes standard JCR assumptions and invokes node.getParent() or something like that.

If we had the line number where the caught exception is thrown that results in the 404 (or the line where we check whether a node exists) it would be easier to debug the issue.

The access error is most likely coming from:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/modeshape/rdf/impl/VersionsRdfContext.java

It appears that the error is generated once the response is ready and is being written out by the RdfStreamProvider.

A section of catalina.out for a request

I'm not sure what is changing between the accumulation of the Rdf and the outputting. Will look closer at RdfStreamingOutputProvider.

The RdfStreams are lazy-loaded. In other words, the content of the various streams are only read when they are used (i.e. when creating the HTTP response). The RdfStreamingOutputProvider shows the error because it is the code that is running through the lazy streams. The actual access error is coming from the VersionsRdfContext... when its stream is actually read.

renderedFields.description:
When using WebAC, if a non-admin user tries to access a resource to which that should have permission AND that resource has versions, a 404 is returned.
Note: admin users have no issue.

To reproduce:

  • Create acl/authorization:
    ===========
    PREFIX acl: <http://www.w3.org/ns/auth/acl#>
    PREFIX pcdm: <http://pcdm.org/models#>

INSERT

{ <> a acl:Authorization ; acl:accessToClass pcdm:Object ; acl:mode acl:Read, acl:Write; acl:agent “testuser” . }

WHERE { }
===========

  • Create a resource of type "pcdm:Object" and link to the acl:
    ===========
    PREFIX acl: <http://www.w3.org/ns/auth/acl#>
    PREFIX pcdm: <http://pcdm.org/models#>

INSERT

{ <> a pcdm:Object; acl:accessControl </fcrepo/rest/my-acls/acl> }

WHERE { }
===========

  • Create a version of the resource
    ===========
    curl -ufedoraAdmin:secret3 -i -XPOST -H"slug: v0" localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/resource/fcr:versions
    ===========
  • Access the resource as "fedoraAdmin" – works
    ===========
    curl -ufedoraAdmin:secret3 -i localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/resource
    ===========
  • Access the resource as "testuser" – FAILS with at 404
    ===========
    curl -utestuser:password1 -i localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/resource
    ===========
